questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Sample 2601: A solution has absorbance 0.496 in a 0.5 cm cell with molar absorptivity 1950 L mol−1 cm−1. What is its concentration in mol/L?

options.misconception: shifts the decimal place by a factor of ten when dividing
shifts the decimal place the opposite way when dividing
ignores the path length in the Beer-Lambert relation

questions.explanation: Beer-Lambert law states A equals epsilon times path length times concentration, so concentration equals absorbance divided by the product of epsilon and path length. Omitting path length or inverting the relation misapplies the law.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Trial 2645: A solution has absorbance 1.143 in a 0.5 cm cell with molar absorptivity 983 L mol−1 cm−1. What is its concentration in mol/L?

options.misconception: shifts the decimal place by a factor of ten when dividing
shifts the decimal place the opposite way when dividing
ignores the path length in the Beer-Lambert relation

questions.explanation: Beer-Lambert law states A equals epsilon times path length times concentration, so concentration equals absorbance divided by the product of epsilon and path length. Omitting path length or inverting the relation misapplies the law.
